name: Conformance Checking
author: Promenade Team
description: Replays a log against a Petri net two ways: alignments (the cheapest explanation of every trace variant, with fitness and escaping-edges precision) and token-based replay (a linear walk that attributes missing and remaining tokens to individual places).

actions.label: Conformance checking (alignments)
actions.description: For every distinct trace variant, the cheapest alignment of sync, log and model moves against the net, plus the fitness and precision derived from it.

agent.whenToUse: The exact answer to "does this model explain this log", and the only one of the two that can say what the *cheapest* explanation of a deviating trace was. Reports precision as well as fitness.
agent.notFor: A large model with heavy concurrency — the search is bounded and reports such variants as unreachable rather than hanging. Use token-based replay there, and for a place-level diagnosis of where the log breaks.
examples: Check this inductive-miner net against the log it was mined from
variantLimit 200 for a quick read on the most frequent behaviour

variantLimit.title: Variant limit
variantLimit.description: Aligns at most this many distinct trace variants, most frequent first.

maxActivities.title: Activity limit
maxActivities.description: Unlike a discovery miner, truncating this silently drops an activity from every trace that has it, producing a wrong alignment rather than an approximate one — set high enough to cover the log's real activity count.

actions.label: Conformance checking (token replay)
actions.description: Fires every trace through the net, inventing a token wherever a transition is not enabled and counting what is left over at the end. Reports token-based fitness and, per place, where the log and the model disagreed.

agent.whenToUse: A fast fitness figure on a model alignments cannot handle, and the only action that localises a deviation to a *place* in the net rather than to a position in a move sequence. Linear in the log: no state-space cap, nothing that can fail to terminate.
agent.notFor: The authoritative fitness number. It never backtracks, so on a net with duplicate labels or heavy concurrency it can report a better figure than the true optimum; use alignments when the number itself is the claim. It also computes no precision.
examples: Replay the log on this net and tell me which places accumulate missing tokens
Which activities could only fire by inventing a token?

variantLimit.title: Variant limit
variantLimit.description: Replays at most this many distinct trace variants, most frequent first. Higher than the alignment default because replay is linear, not a search.

maxActivities.title: Activity limit
maxActivities.description: Truncating this drops an activity from every trace that has it, which silently improves the fitness instead of approximating it — set high enough to cover the log's real activity count.

citation.text: van der Aalst, W.M.P., Adriansyah, A., van Dongen, B.F. (2012). Replaying History on Process Models for Conformance Checking and Performance Analysis. WIREs Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery, 2(2), 182-192.
